correctness.rationale: Every pair of off-fiber vertices in a generating neighborhood has a unique center because H has no C4, yielding an explicit full free-face matching with a closed-form pair count. The residual complex is the exact union of edge blocks. Each half-block retracts relative to its fiber-boundary sphere, and its crown-graph intersection has cycle rank q_m. Since m≥4, the two maps from each crown graph to the simply connected fiber spheres are null; cofibration and homotopy-colimit replacements lead to the claimed integral wedge, with no reliance on finite extrapolation. The included standard-library checker reconstructs adjacency, verifies every matching pair and core, and computes exact mod-two homology in 14 cases.

The broader general-base clique-fiber calculation instead concerns closed-neighborhood Čech, a mathematically different complex with unequal sphere multiplicities.
